description: FBS (Fahrplanbearbeitungssystem, timetable processing system) is a commercial software package for railway timetable construction developed by iRFP, an engineering office in Dresden focused on railway operations that links university research with practice. According to iRFP it covers timetable construction, vehicle circulation optimisation, resource planning and reuse of the resulting data, and is used for long-term strategic service planning, for preparing regional rail tenders by transport authorities, and in daily operations of passenger and freight railways. Its main modules are combined in the iPLAN planning software, with a railML interface, an interface to the electronic train path ordering of DB, and other converters. A newer OpenStreetMap converter builds FBS infrastructure networks from public map data for Germany and other countries, including closed or dismantled lines, which helps reactivation studies. Coverage: any network, mainly German-speaking users. Access: licensed software; product pages are in German. Licence and cost: proprietary and paid, with conditions on request. Caveats: no public data, and documentation is aimed at customers. It supports timetable and capacity planning for rail and regional transit. It relates to Viriato, OpenRailwayMap and OpenStreetMap in the catalogue.
